messages:
mike_support: Hey team — just triaging a month-end support case from Acme (acct: acme-corp-44). They say the invoice total is ~14% higher than the dashboard for Feb. Invoice INV-2026-02 shows a distinct 'Pro Tier' line with 2.1M tokens; dashboard shows 1.84M. Screenshot + CSV attached by customer: https://files.acme.example/INV-2026-02-snapshot.csv

rachel_billing: Ack — can you paste the invoice line items and the dashboard export? Any credits or plan changes around cutoff?

mike_support: Pasted CSV snippet from customer below. No plan change in their billing history until Mar 5. They are on Pro monthly.
```csv
line_item, tokens, unit_price, total
pro_tier,2100000,0.0008,1680.00
overage,0,0.0012,0.00
credit,-50.00,-50.00
```

samir_engineer: Can you run the metering reconciliation query for that account for Feb? key fields: event_id, timestamp, model, tokens. Look for duplicate event_id or writes after cutoff. I'll drop a quick query to run.

jess_ops: opsbot: Did nightly-metering-backfill run for Feb on 2026-03-01?

opsbot: nightly-metering-backfill finished at 2026-03-01T00:03:12Z. Processed file: s3://redwood-metering/backfill/2026-02/part-09.csv (rows: 124k). No errors reported.

samir_engineer: Thanks. mike, can you paste results from this query (run against prod metering):
```sql
SELECT event_id, account_id, sum(tokens) as tokens_sum, count(*) as occurrences
FROM metering.events
WHERE account_id = 'acme-corp-44' AND timestamp >= '2026-02-01' AND timestamp < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY event_id, account_id
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY occurrences DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

mike_support: Ran it and got 3 event_id rows with occurrences = 2, each ~1200-1800 tokens. Full result pasted:
```
| event_id        | tokens_sum | occurrences |
| evt_9a2f3b      | 2400       | 2          |
| evt_72c1eaa     | 3600       | 2          |
| evt_ff01be      | 2400       | 2          |
```

rachel_billing: That would explain the delta (~8400 tokens + others?). But their invoice delta is ~260k tokens. Any larger duplicates?

samir_engineer: Good catch. Those three are small. We should also check for a batch-level duplicate where the entire file was processed twice. Check ingestion logs for file checksum/ingest_id for that s3 path.

jess_ops: opsbot: show ingest-log s3://redwood-metering/backfill/2026-02/part-09.csv

opsbot: ingest-log: part-09.csv processed by backfill-run-2026-03-01-0003 (ingest_id: bf-20260301-0003). Previous ingest entry for same file found: backfill-run-2026-02-28-2359 (ingest_id: bf-20260228-2359). Both reported success. Checksums: bf-0003 sha256=abcd1234, bf-2359 sha256=abcd1234 (match).

samir_engineer: That's the smoking gun — same file processed twice across the cutoff boundary. Because our metering pipeline didn't dedupe on file-level ingest_id, we double-wrote rows for that file. Need to dedupe by event_id at write time AND add a file-ingest id check. For immediate remediation: remove duplicate rows for that ingest_id pair for acme-corp-44 and re-run invoice recompute.

rachel_billing: Agree. mike, please request an invoices re-computation after ops rollback. Also confirm whether credits were applied incorrectly.

mike_support: On it. Opening a Jira for rollback + recompute: RED-INV-1421. Action: jess to run de-dupe script and mark invoice for recompute.

jess_ops: I'll run the de-dupe now. Command I'll execute: 
```bash
python ops/de_dupe_metering.py --account acme-corp-44 --file part-09.csv --ingest-ids bf-20260228-2359,bf-20260301-0003 --dry-run=false
```

jess_ops: Running...

opsbot: job bf-dedupe-2067890123 started by jess_ops at 2026-03-01T01:22:10Z

jess_ops: Completed. Script removed 254,212 duplicate token rows (total tokens reclaimed: 266,400). Took ~2m 18s.

mike_support: Thanks, can billing kick off recompute+regen invoice?

rachel_billing: Kicked off invoice recompute job INV-2026-02 for account acme-corp-44. Expect new invoice in ~15m. Noting internal postmortem: backfill runner shouldn't schedule the same file twice across midnight.

samir_engineer: I'll put an emergency PR to add an ingest_id uniqueness constraint and a reconciliation check that flags same checksum processed twice within 6 hours.

mike_support: Customer notified: "We've found duplicated metering rows caused by a backfill file processed twice during the cutoff window. We're removing duplicates and regenerating the invoice. We'll follow up when it's done." :white_check_mark:

opsbot: invoice-regenerate job INV-2026-02 started at 2026-03-01T01:42:21Z, status: success. New invoice total matches dashboard within 0.5% (invoice: 1,845,320 tokens vs dashboard: 1,844,900 tokens).

rachel_billing: Closing on customer once they confirm. Postmortem planned, and ticket RED-OPS-339 to prevent duplicate backfill scheduling.

mike_support: I'll update the case. Thanks all. :tada:
